coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Parcel A
record.summary: Phase 1 office parcel at 20th and Maryland Streets, entitled for roughly 350,000 gross square feet of commercial office over retail and underground parking; appraised in 2020 at $66 million for a 99-year prepaid lease, but Brookfield declined to proceed in June 2020 and no vertical development has started. King Street Properties announced a life-science plan for it in 2023.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. Current design (DES Architects + Grimshaw, ~356,000-365,000 GSF, for King Street Properties' life-science program) superseded an earlier (2019) Hacker Architects + Quezada Architecture mass-timber office design (~300,000-310,000 sf, billed as one of the largest CLT office buildings in North America) -- both designs are real, the mass-timber one was simply replaced, not fabricated. No construction-start source found.

open_questions: No construction start, building permit or vertical DDA for this parcel was found in any Port Commission document through the August 11, 2026 informational report, which says the developer 'has not exercised an option of any Phase 1 option parcels'.

Per-parcel gross square footage and unit counts are not published in the D4D (which sets height, stories and land-use scenarios, not parcel programs); the SUD's per-parcel programs would be in the SUD ordinance (Planning Code Sec. 249.79) or the Phase Submittal, neither of which was retrieved.

Whether the King Street Properties partnership is still in effect: the Port's June 2025 deck speaks of the life-science effort in the past tense ('prior to collapse of that industry') and the July 2026 Real Deal report describes a 300,000 sq ft office building, not a lab.
The Feb 2020 staff memo says Parcel A is entitled for ~350,000 GSF while Resolution 20-07's recital says ~240,000 GSF; which figure the DDA option actually carries is unresolved.

An earlier (2019) mass-timber office design by Hacker Architects with Quezada Architecture is recorded in this parcel's geometry file; the architects' pages returned 404/empty during this pass, so it is not restated here.
Construction cost estimates for the office building: none found.
